messages.author: fd5b3eee58ac5e83
messages.subject: mesh and adjacency matrix
parts:
Hello
I am new to R-INLA. I have a dataset spanning 100 polygons (I.e. for each postal codes -> lattice data). I am running a besag model for the regional component with a rw1 for the time component

response ~ 1 +f(region, model = 'bym', graph = adj) + f(time, model = 'rw1') + f(time.unstr, model = 'iid')

following Biangiardo (2013) (Spatial and spatio-temporal models with R-INLA). 

The example I was following used an adjacency matrix, and it actually works fine. However, I now want to include a seasonal effect and the examples I find for this (https://ourcodingclub.github.io/2018/12/04/inla.html) used a mesh and stacking. My questions:

1) Do I need to stack my relatively simple model setup?
2) Do I need a mesh if I have an adjacency matrix (lattice data, not point data)?

I see why a mesh is necessary for point-data, but I don't understand what the mesh does in the case of lattice data (if it is needed).

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh and adjacency matrix
parts:
Hi,

1) Adjacency graphs are for discretised space, and meshes are for continuous space, so no, you don’t need to involve a mesh.
2) stacks are never strictly needed, they are just convenient when constructing some types of model. In your case you can probably make it work without them, since you just need to construct the “group” index vector. However, you can also use stacks in a simplified way to the mesh models; essentially just ignore most of the mesh related stuff and replace the mesh.index output with your regular graph index vector when calling inla.stack;
 Alternatively, you can even call inla.spde.make.A without a mesh; instead, supply “index” and “group”. This needs to be combined with inla.spde.make.index to make the canonical index vectors for the latent model.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh and adjacency matrix
parts:
Thank you very much for the explanation!!

Can I just

(1) add the month (1-12) as a group-index to the date?

response ~ 1 +f(region, model = 'bym', graph = adj) + f(time, model = 'rw1', group = month) + f(time.unstr, model = 'iid')

(2)  or in a separate month model?

response ~ 1 +f(region, model = 'bym', graph = adj) + f(time, model = 'rw1') + f(time.unstr, model = 'iid') + 
f(month, model = 'rw1', group = month, control. group = list(model = 'iid')

(3) or something like that, adapted from a code you provided to another answer for '...each location different seasonal shape'

response ~ 1 +f(region, model = 'bym', graph = adj) + f(time, model = 'rw1') + f(time.unstr, model = 'iid') +
   f(month, model = 'rw1', replicate = region)

Best regards,
Brigitte

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh and adjacency matrix
parts:
Hi,

Both 1 and 2 are possible options; version 2 will have to work a bit
harder to separate the common effect from the grouped effects; the
model is only identifiable due to the priors; 1 may therefore be more
stable.

Finn
